findings.title: Record and contain the privileged mount helper before starting it
findings.evidence: subprocess.run(argv,check=True,timeout=30) invokes docker run --rm; no full container ID is retained and no finally/timeout containment follows. The receipt is written only after that call succeeds.
findings.consequence: If the Docker client times out after daemon acceptance, the privileged host-namespace nsenter/mount helper can remain running after preparation exits. The campaign prepare intent prevents a repeat, but does not contain that original helper or establish whether its mount happened.

validation.method: Executed the actual bind_workspace() against a canonical temporary private workspace, sparse size-bound image fixture and mocked losetup/Docker acceptance; no Docker or privileged operations occurred.

findings.suggested_fix: Separate docker create from start, validate and durably retain the full image/label/name-bound ID before start, and contain only that original helper after start/wait uncertainty. Preserve the mount state and workspace preimage for reconciliation; never automatically unmount, retry or recreate an ambiguous operation.
